[L438-L456] (MED/interpolation-contract) Prescribed-bathymetry timestamps are not checked for ordering or coverage of time zero, and the interpolation status returned in dummy is ignored when constructing the initial bed.
[L524,L533-L535,L546-L598] (MED/uninitialized-arrays) wave_init allocates Dp, umwci, vmwci, and zswci but the subsequent initialization block never assigns them.
[L683-L687] (MED/input-error-handling) spectral_wave_init opens the boundary file and reads its header without IOSTAT handling, despite later records having explicit format-error checks.

[L781,L820-L829,L844-L848,L879-L973] (MED/uninitialized-arrays) flow_init allocates qmag, dUi, dVi, cfu, cfv, zs1, sigz, and the vertical-profile arrays but does not initialize them in its extensive initialization block.

[L1076-L1156] (HIGH/division-by-zero) The hotstartflow iteration divides by s%cf even though flow_init explicitly set s%cf to zero and has not computed a friction coefficient before entering this block.

[L1076-L1156] (HIGH/conditional-parameter-use) The hotstartflow force balance unconditionally uses rhoa, Cd, windsu, and windnv although rhoa/Cd are read only when wind is enabled and no wind-disabled guard is present here.

[L1104-L1156] (MED/nontermination) The stationary-flow fixed-point loop has no iteration limit or non-finite residual check, so a divergent or NaN-producing initialization can run indefinitely or exit with invalid state.

[L1211-L1215] (HIGH/disabled-logic) For a completely wet domain under instantaneous tide, the only code intended to populate zs0fac is commented out, leaving both tide weights at the earlier all-zero initialization.

[L1325-L1329] (LOW/conditional-initialization) D15 is always allocated but assigned only when dilatancy is enabled, leaving the array undefined in the other configuration even though it remains part of distributed state.

[L1332-L1341,L1384-L1387] (MED/model-inconsistency) Single-fraction sediment forces every layer thickness to at least 10 m, whereas multi-fraction sediment uses dzg1/dzg2/dzg3 directly, creating a large unexplained behavior change solely from ngd.

[L1367-L1377] (MED/input-validation) Sediment-fraction normalization handles a near-zero total but never rejects negative individual fractions, so a positive total containing negatives is normalized into still-negative bed fractions.

[L1309-L1318,L1425-L1462] (MED/uninitialized-arrays) sed_init allocates iwl, Tsg, vmag, ccz, ca, and refA but omits them from the subsequent initialization assignments (iwl is notably adjacent to initialized istruct).
[L1580-L1594] (MED/bounds) For a v-oriented discharge in a ny==0 model, the n1 clamp first raises the index to 1 and then lowers it to s%ny==0, storing a zero grid index in pdisch.

[L1658-L1666] (MED/bounds) Drifter indices are formed by adding unconstrained fractional offsets to the nearest grid index and converting to integer without clamping, so out-of-domain drifter coordinates can produce indices outside the arrays.

[L1795-L1801,L1819-L1825,L1843-L1851] (HIGH/input-error-handling) All low-level hotstart readers capture OPEN/READ IOSTAT but never inspect it, allowing format or I/O failures to leave restart fields partially undefined after existence/length checks pass.

listX.text: [L323-L339] (HIGH/dimension-validation) fftn truncates an overlong dim list but never validates each dimension index or rejects duplicates, so zero/out-of-range entries index shape illegally and repeated entries are transformed/scaled multiple times.
[L331-L339] (HIGH/shape-validation) fftn does not require positive shape entries or guard PRODUCT overflow before using the product for scaling, loop bounds, and transform strides.
[L337-L342,L348-L372] (HIGH/uninitialized-status) fftradix returns immediately for npass<=1 without defining optional INTENT(OUT) stat, after which fftn tests that undefined status value.
[L323-L343] (MED/empty-transform-status) When a present dim array has zero length, fftn performs no fftradix call and never defines the caller's optional INTENT(OUT) stat.
[L976-L999] (HIGH/zero-size) hilbert evaluates log(real(m)) and derives an FFT allocation size without checking m>0, so a zero-length input enters log(0) and invalid integer/exponent calculations.
[L983,L999] (MED/data-loss) hilbert accepts a complex input array but explicitly copies only real(xi) into the transform buffer, silently discarding any imaginary component.

[L1099-L1128] (HIGH/bounds-and-axis) flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension and assigns whole columns, causing out-of-bounds access when M1>M2 and duplicating column-flip behavior instead of flipping rows.
[L1235-L1263] (LOW/nonfinite-input) xerf maps NaN inputs to +1 because both magnitude comparisons are false and the fallback branch is selected, masking the non-finite input.
[L1288-L1293] (MED/integer-overflow) random seeds with iabs(j) without handling the most-negative integer, whose absolute value is not representable and can leave an invalid negative seed.

listY.text: [L323-L332,L337-L339] (MED/unchecked dimension contract) fftn neither rejects nor reports zero, duplicate, or out-of-range dim entries (and silently truncates an oversized dim array), allowing invalid shape indexing, repeated transforms, or a zero-length normalization product.

[L337-L341,L348-L353,L372] (HIGH/undefined output status) fftradix returns for npass <= 1 without defining its INTENT(OUT) optional stat, after which fftn reads that undefined value when stat is present.
[L323-L345] (MED/undefined output status) When a present dim array has size zero, fftn performs no fftradix call and returns without ever defining its INTENT(OUT) stat argument.

[L331-L338] (MED/integer overflow / bounds contract) The products of caller-provided shape values are computed in default integer without validation, so nonpositive or overflowing extents can produce invalid scaling and assumed-size array traversal.
[L976-L1018] (MED/input-domain contract) hilbert accepts m without validation, and m <= 0 reaches log(real(m)) and subsequent invalid exponent/allocation/index calculations.

[L983,L999] (LOW/unclear data contract) hilbert declares xi complex but deliberately initializes the transform from only real(xi), silently discarding any input imaginary component without documenting that xi must represent real data.
[L1002,L1016] (LOW/precision loss) hilbert computes both normalization factors through default-real real(n) and sqrt rather than fftkind precision.

[L1117-L1121] (HIGH/array-bounds / dimension defect) flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension temp3a(:,ii) and M1+1-ii, so a nonsquare M1-by-M2 array can be indexed out of bounds or only partly assigned and the branch does not actually reverse the first dimension.

[L1288-L1293] (LOW/integer edge case) random applies iabs to an unrestricted default integer seed, for which the most-negative representable integer is not representable after negation and can yield overflow or a nonpositive seed.

listX.text: [L21-L28] (LOW/undefined pointer state) parameter pointer components have no default NULL() association, leaving unused components undefined or stale across descriptor reuse.

[L76-L100] (MED/shared-result aliasing) Every getkey result of a given type points to one module-saved scratch scalar, so a later call silently changes the value observed through all earlier descriptors and the routine is not reentrant or thread-safe.

[L88-L100] (MED/incomplete result metadata) Successful getkey calls set only name, rank, type, and one value pointer, leaving the public units, description, dimensions, and nonselected pointer fields undefined or inherited from a previous use.

listY.text: [L13-L29,L88-L100] (MED/pointer-state) parameter pointer components have no default NULL initialization, and getkey associates only the pointer matching the current type, leaving the other pointer components with undefined or stale association state.

[L76-L100] (MED/aliasing-contract) All returned scalar pointers alias one of three shared SAVE temporaries, so a later getkey call of the same type silently changes the value observed through every earlier result and makes the API non-reentrant.

[L44-L63] (LOW/case-consistency) Introspection key lookup is case-sensitive even though the parameter-file reader performs case-insensitive key matching, creating two different naming contracts for the same parameters.

[L13-L19,L88-L100] (LOW/incomplete-metadata) The exported parameter type advertises units, description, and dimension metadata, but getkey initializes none of those fields for a successful scalar lookup.

listX.text: [L49-L65] (MED/MPI result inconsistency) check_file_exist performs the inquiry only on xmaster without broadcasting error, so a present exist output is always reported true on non-master ranks regardless of the file's existence.

[L70-L149] (MED/unchecked I/O and allocation) The three check_file_length variants do not validate extents or capture allocation/open errors, so bad dimensions or an inaccessible file can trigger a raw runtime failure before their intended read-error reporting.

[L163-L176,L227-L246] (MED/uninitialized dispatch state) checkbcfilelength does not assign filetype for wbctype values outside its enumerated branches, yet immediately selects on filetype, whose dummy argument has no declared intent or local default.

[L197-L224] (MED/empty-list validation gap) A LOCLIST file containing only its header produces nlocs=0 and skips all boundary-duration validation, allowing a positive-duration simulation to pass this check without any boundary file.

[L295-L321] (MED/fixed-unit collision) get_file_length opens hard-coded unit 11 without checking whether it is already connected, unlike the module's own free-unit allocator, risking interference with unrelated open files or an open failure.

[L315-L321] (LOW/unchecked I/O classification) get_file_length does not capture OPEN errors and treats every nonzero READ iostat as ordinary end-of-file, so malformed numeric input is silently reported as a shorter file.

[L345-L360] (HIGH/resource-id exhaustion) create_new_fid_generic's initialized local tryunit has implicit SAVE and only decreases across calls, so closed units are never reconsidered and the allocator eventually reports exhaustion after enough cumulative opens even when nearly all units are free.

listY.text: [L49-L65] (MED/mpi-consistency) File existence is checked only on xmaster and the error flag is never broadcast, so non-master callers requesting the optional exist result always report true even when the master found the file missing.

[L81-L93,L109-L121,L136-L148] (MED/input-error-handling) The check_file_length overloads open files without OPEN IOSTAT handling, so permission/open failures are reported only indirectly through a subsequent read.

[L79-L85,L106-L113,L133-L140] (LOW/precision-contract) Length/validity checks parse scientific input into default-real temporary arrays even though the consuming model generally reads real*8, so values valid in double precision can fail or overflow during the preliminary check.

[L70-L149] (LOW/misnamed-contract) check_file_length verifies only that at least the requested number of numeric values can be read and never detects trailing records/values, despite its name suggesting an exact dimensional check.

[L141-L143] (LOW/diagnostic) The 3D error path passes the error text as writelog's format argument rather than supplying the empty format argument used by the 1D and 2D overloads, yielding an inconsistent/malformed diagnostic call.

[L197-L220] (MED/record-counting) LOCLIST sets nlocs to every remaining physical line, including blank/comment lines, and then requires each to parse as a location record, with no filtering or declared file-format guard.
[L295-L325] (MED/unit-collision) get_file_length uses hard-coded unit 11 rather than create_new_fid, so it can close or conflict with another file already connected to that unit.

[L295-L325] (MED/misnamed-contract) get_file_length stops counting at the first nonnumeric/failed list-directed record and counts numeric records rather than physical lines, making the generic name misleading and malformed later records indistinguishable from end-of-file.

[L345-L360] (LOW/unit-allocation-contract) create_new_fid_generic can return the same unit on consecutive calls if the first caller has not opened it yet, because it reserves no unit and retains only a shared probe value.

listX.text: [L82-L101,L104-L121] (MED/index-validation) index_allocate and index_allocated do not validate index or reject an unknown choice, unlike indextos, so invalid requests can silently no-op or report a scalar-like allocated result.
[L329-L336] (MED/selector-contract) space_distribute_vector treats every selector other than lowercase 'x' as 'y', allowing typos or unsupported selectors to choose the wrong decomposition silently.
[L707-L729] (MED/memory-leak) The btype '2' distribution path allocates vectorg on every rank but deallocates it only on xmaster, leaking the pointer allocation on each non-master invocation.

[L760-L768] (LOW/sentinel-contract) space_who_has returns the undocumented magic value -123 when no computational domain contains a coordinate and emits no diagnostic, leaving callers to infer failure.

[L980-L1005] (LOW/dead-selector) All four loc cases in space_collect_vector_real8 execute the identical collection and there is no default case, so loc currently has no semantic effect while invalid values silently do nothing.

[L1083-L1101,L1147-L1156] (HIGH/bounds) space_collect_mnem passes chartoindex's -1 failure result to space_collect_index, which indexes sg%collected(index) before the later indextos range check can reject it.

[L1114-L1135] (HIGH/false-success) Real variables of unhandled rank (notably rank 1) and unknown real cases fall through without collection but are still marked sg%collected(index)=.true., suppressing future attempts.

[L1079-L1092,L1131-L1133] (LOW/instrumentation) The collection end marker logs event_coll_start again, and the already-collected early return skips an end marker entirely, producing unbalanced or mislabeled MPE traces.

[L1186-L1189] (MED/distributed-grid-contract) gridprops labels xzg11/yzg11 as the global grid origin but assigns them from the local array element (1,1), which is not the global origin on non-top/non-left MPI subdomains unless callers prevent local invocation.
[L1335-L1399] (MED/division-by-zero) Grid-cell inverse areas are formed by unconditional division by computed polygon areas (or metric products) with no local degeneracy/zero-area guard.

listY.text: [L65-L101,L104-L122] (LOW/inconsistent index validation) index_allocate and index_allocated do not validate index as indextos does, and an invalid index can silently no-op or be reported allocated because the default result is true.
[L78-L101] (LOW/unchecked string contract) index_allocate unconditionally takes choice(1:1), which is invalid for a zero-length actual argument, and silently ignores nonempty unsupported choices.

[L306-L365] (LOW/asymmetric API contract) space_distribute_vector treats every xy value other than lowercase 'x' as a y distribution, while space_distribute_block_vector accepts only lowercase 'y' and aborts for all other values.

[L440-L521,L578-L588] (MED/subdomain-size contract) The MPI decomposition subtracts fixed two-cell borders and immediately allocates local state without checking that every lm and ln is large enough, so an over-decomposed small grid can produce inverted computational ranges.
[L745-L770] (LOW/unreported lookup failure) space_who_has returns the undocumented sentinel -123 when a point has no owning computational region and provides no status or diagnostic.

[L1065-L1087,L1135] (MED/unchecked collection index) space_collect_index uses index directly in sg%collected before indextos can validate it, and space_collect_mnem passes through chartoindex results without checking for an unknown mnemonic.

[L1114-L1129,L1135] (HIGH/false collection state) For real rank-1 arrays and unsupported real ranks/types, space_collect_index performs no collection yet still marks sg%collected(index) true, suppressing future attempts.

[L1175-L1253,L1402-L1419] (MED/minimum-grid bounds) gridprops assumes nx>=1 throughout and requires nx>=2 to define alfaz from an interior point; with nx=1 its two boundary-copy assignments merely circulate an uninitialized orientation.

[L1335-L1398] (HIGH/degenerate-cell division) gridprops inverts computed cell areas, and in 1D products of metrics, without rejecting zero-area or repeated-coordinate cells, producing infinite geometric factors.

[L1453-L1529] (MED/empty computational ranges) ranges_init can produce lower bounds greater than upper bounds for small global or local nx/ny values, with no validation before those ranges are consumed by array sections and reductions.

listX.text: [L10-L33] (MED/pointer-state) Every rank/type pointer in arraytype lacks default NULL initialization, so consumers cannot safely query association state on a newly created descriptor before the construction code explicitly initializes all unused alternatives.

listY.text: [L21-L31] (LOW/undefined pointer state) arraytype's mutually exclusive pointer components have no default NULL() initialization, so newly declared descriptors contain undefined association status for every component not explicitly set by generated mapping code.
[L37-L49] (MED/error-signaling contract) chartoindex reports an unknown name only by logging and returns -1 as an ordinary index, leaving callers able to subscript arrays with that invalid value.

listX.text: [L1041-L1045] (MED/wrong-state-field) The slopecorr parmapply call stores its selected-name string in par%sedfricfac_str, overwriting the string field for a different parameter instead of a slope-correction string field.

[L1252,L2131-L2136] (LOW/range-contract) nglobalvar input is capped at 20, while the built-in default path installs 21 global variables, leaving the explicit-input capacity contract inconsistent with the default.

[L1359-L1383] (MED/conditional-initialization) The Snell-law default calculation reads thetamin, thetamax, and dtheta whenever single_dir is zero, although this routine assigns those directional-grid fields only inside the earlier swave==1 branch.
[L1514-L1519] (LOW/conditional-initialization) Depth scaling modifies par%maxerror unconditionally, although maxerror is assigned here only for stationary waves or single_dir mode.

[L1633-L1655] (MED/unsupported-configuration) The block says it only allows Baldock/Janssen in stationary mode and Roelvink formulations otherwise, but non-stationary Baldock or Janssen selections merely produce warnings and are neither rejected nor changed.

[L1710-L1714] (LOW/boundary-condition) The tide/epsi post-check tests epsi < -1 even though the configured default is exactly -1, so the documented automatic-computation notice is skipped for the default sentinel.
[L1850-L1852] (LOW/diagnostic) The wave-current warning is entered for WAVEMODEL_STATIONARY but states that interaction with non-stationary waves is experimental.

[L2009-L2018,L2051-L2097] (MED/mpi-portability) distribute_par broadcasts the raw bytes of a derived type containing pointer descriptors and then repairs only three named pointers, a representation-dependent contract that is unsafe if the type gains other descriptor-bearing fields or MPI ranks differ in layout.

[L2457-L2464] (MED/input-error-handling) readPointPosition searches indefinitely for the section keyword using reads without IOSTAT, so a missing/malformed section reaches EOF without a controlled read error or termination path.

[L2541-L2547] (LOW/diagnostic) The backward-compatibility warning emitted when the legacy nonh parameter is present says nonh was specified using wavemodel, reversing the actual parameter relationship.

listY.text: [L145-L167,L301-L315] (HIGH/parameter-order defect) The XBeach grid branch decides whether a depth file is required from par%hotstart before the hotstart parameter is read from params.txt, so a requested hotstart can follow stale/default state and unnecessarily require or load depfile.

[L170-L175,L247-L266,L283-L296,L419-L434] (HIGH/advisory-only critical bounds) Critical positive quantities including dx, dy, dtheta, dtheta_s, tstop, gravity, and wave periods are read without strict=.true., so zero or negative out-of-range values only warn and can later drive divisions, invalid extents, or nonterminating angle normalization.

[L193-L237] (MED/unchecked external grid dimensions) Delft3D mmax and nmax are converted directly to nx=mmax-1 and ny=nmax-1 without validating minimum or maximum grid sizes before downstream allocation and boundary indexing.

[L733] (LOW/suspicious parameter key) The dynamicroughness lookup embeds a trailing blank in the key literal, unlike the externally documented spelling and neighboring lookups, relying on blank-padding equality for recognition.
[L737-L742] (MED/inconsistent friction bounds) maxcf and mincf are read independently without enforcing mincf<=maxcf, permitting an inverted clamp interval.

[L1041-L1045] (MED/wrong metadata target) The slopecorr parmapply call stores its selected option string into par%sedfricfac_str, overwriting the sediment-friction description instead of a slope-correction field.
[L1187-L1190] (MED/morphology time-order contract) morstart and morstop are bounded independently but never checked for morstop>=morstart, allowing an inverted morphology interval.

[L1227-L1248] (HIGH/zero output interval accepted) tint, tintg, tintp, tintm, and tinth use strict lower bounds of zero, allowing zero intervals that timestep_init later uses as divisors when generating schedules.

[L1536-L1538] (LOW/nonlinear option coercion) Every posdwn value below 0.1, including allowed small positive values, is coerced to -1 while other positive magnitudes remain unnormalized, making this nominal sign option behave discontinuously.

[L1709-L1714] (LOW/boundary-condition threshold) The tide auto-epsi branch tests epsi<-1 even though the configured default is exactly -1, so the documented automatic path is not entered at the default sentinel.
[L1848-L1853] (LOW/inverted diagnostic) The warning text says wave-current interaction with non-stationary waves is experimental, but the condition emits it only for the stationary wave model.

[L1937-L1954] (MED/conditional-state dependence) Post-processing unconditionally reads tintg, tintp, tintm, tinth, wavint, morfac, morstart, morstop, and rt although several are assigned in all_input only under feature-specific branches, leaving correctness dependent on hidden defaults in the generated parameter declaration.

[L2009-L2019] (HIGH/nonportable MPI serialization) distribute_par broadcasts raw sizeof(par) bytes for a non-C-interoperable Fortran derived type containing pointer descriptors, copying process-local addresses and compiler-dependent representation across ranks before repairing only selected pointers.

[L2124-L2166] (MED/output-count inconsistency) The documented/default nglobalvar limit is 20, but the default global-output branch writes 21 names and sets nglobalvar=21, creating an inconsistent public count contract.

[L2323-L2415] (MED/case-sensitive parser inconsistency) readOutputStrings searches parameter keys with exact case and without strippedline normalization even though the main readkey parser is case-insensitive, so inputs accepted for the count can fail when their following variable list is located.
[L2366-L2399,L2454-L2521] (MED/fixed-unit collision) Output-list and point-position readers open hard-coded unit 10 rather than obtaining a free unit, risking collision with another connected file.

[L2454-L2464] (HIGH/unchecked EOF) readPointPosition searches indefinitely with external READ statements that have no iostat, so a missing or differently cased count keyword terminates on raw end-of-file instead of reporting a controlled input error.
